hints: Look carefully at the two features of the graph separately, the steepness at the start and the final flat level.
Curve Y starts less steep than X but finishes higher, so the rate is slower but the total amount of oxygen is greater.
Think about what change gives more moles of hydrogen peroxide in total but at a lower overall concentration.
walkthrough:
**Read what the graph tells us**

Curve Y has a gentler initial slope than curve X, so the initial rate is slower. But Y levels off at a higher volume, so more oxygen is made in total.

Remember: slope = rate, plateau height = total moles of product.

**Link plateau height to moles**

The decomposition is:
$$2\text{H}_2\text{O}_2(aq) \rightarrow 2\text{H}_2\text{O}(l) + \text{O}_2(g)$$
More $\text{O}_2$ at the end can only mean more $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ was present at the start. So total moles of $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ must have increased.

**Link initial slope to concentration**

A slower initial rate with the same catalyst and temperature means a lower concentration of $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$. This happens if we add extra volume of a more dilute solution, total moles go up but concentration goes down.

**Conclude the correct alteration**

Adding some $0.1 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ adds extra moles (higher plateau) while diluting the original $1.0 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ solution (slower start). That matches curve Y exactly.

options.A: More manganese(IV) oxide means more catalyst surface, so the rate would be faster and the initial slope steeper. The total moles of H2O2 are unchanged, so the final volume would be the same, not higher.
options.B: Adding dilute 0.1 mol dm-3 H2O2 increases the total moles of H2O2, so more O2 is eventually formed and the plateau is higher. At the same time the overall concentration is lowered by dilution, so the initial rate is slower and the slope is gentler. This gives exactly curve Y.
options.C: Adding water dilutes the H2O2, so the rate would be slower and the slope gentler. However no extra H2O2 is added, so the total moles and final volume of O2 would stay the same, not increase.
options.D: Raising the temperature increases particle kinetic energy and frequency of successful collisions, so the rate would be faster and the slope steeper. The total moles of H2O2 are unchanged, so the final volume would be the same, the opposite of curve Y.
